who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), write-only lane H (hosted start in the child) under D124
what: bstd's `Hosting::new` takes `Vec<String>` and `Vec<(String, String)>` (implicit Global) for the program's arguments and grants, so a host made in the launcher must allocate on the global heap with no allocator named; the launcher's rows in the only-fall ratchets (std-alloc, alloc-sites, ambient-reach's env column for `args_os`/`var_os`/`remove_var`) rise with the piece, and a write-only lane cannot run the ratchet script to rewrite them.
cost: none yet; the coordinator rewrites the rows after the round
cause: Hosting's constructor predates the explicit-allocator rule (D102) for its argument lists
whys: the host's lists are owned strings; Hosting holds `alloc` only for its answers' encodings; the in-process host in blaze-cli program.rs had the same shape and its rows were counted there
class: a shared constructor without an allocator parameter forces every new caller to raise an only-fall ratchet
prevention: wanted: `Hosting::new` takes its argument and grant lists borrowed (or in `alloc`), so the launcher passes the process's argv and the parsed grants in place
workaround: coordinator rewrites the launcher's ratchet rows after compiling
